light_description: Long-running HSW amplifier-inspired overdrive family; surviving records include standard, limited and Super Bass/Fujiyama variants, making it a distinct historical builder/product corridor.
Japanese HSW overdrive documented among the builder's core dirt products; period community records and surviving catalog indexes preserve it as a distinct model.
HSW overdrive model preserved in the surviving product index and specialist documentation; exterior specimen photography is available through secondary listings.
Historical HSW fuzz model documented in the Effects Database catalog; retained as a separate fuzz identity.
Historical HSW fuzz family with later derivative variants; surviving HSW documentation provides transistor-era model descriptions and photographs.
Limited/special HSW fuzz product with surviving specimen photography and user documentation; preserved as a distinct product record.
Handmade Japanese overdrive designed by Keijiro Fukushima and housed in a cast Nambu-tekki iron enclosure; first released in January 2020 after extended enclosure/circuit prototyping.
Japanese handmade overdrive/distortion with three-band EQ, multiple clipping modes and switchable buffer; long-running core A.Y.A product with extensive surviving photographs.
Higher-gain A.Y.A dirt model with three-way distortion/booster/overdrive modes; documented as a companion to Drivesta in the builder's historical lineup.

Toshihiko Tanabe's foundational handmade overdrive, developed from a personal 2007 design request; natural Japanese abalone-top enclosure and hand-wired construction are documented by Tanabe and interview sources.
Tanabe overdrive optimized for single-coil use with three switchable voices; documented as a core handmade order product and associated with Robben Ford.
Tanabe overdrive built around Brian May-oriented voicing, with multiple compression/voice modes and distinctive abalone-top presentation.
Tanabe overdrive developed for Carlos Santana-oriented sustaining lead tones; official documentation lists multiple voicing modes and identifies the model as a core order product.
Three-germanium-transistor Tanabe fuzz aimed at a controlled middle ground between fuzz and distortion; official documentation gives the product description and ordering details.

Tokyo/Yokohama-area boutique overdrive with a documented bipolar-transistor clipping stage and JFET-input architecture; current product photography and specifications are available from specialist documentation.
